answer: Synchronous memory-hard challenges resist Sybil attacks by forcing each agent to traverse an identity-salted DRAM graph on a shared epoch cue and echo a fresh digest before a tight deadline. Because rotating seeds turn prior lookup tables into a useless relic, an adversary cannot spawn a plume of multiplexed clones without dedicating physical RAM capacity and memory bandwidth per identity. However, periodic memory saturation degrades concurrent inference tasks and excludes low-RAM edge devices.
